title: Qualitative characteristics
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:34Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers only relevance and faithful representation, alongside the entity and going concern assumptions, so it lacks the enhancing characteristics of comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability that this point teaches.

draft.title: Qualitative characteristics
card: Qualitative characteristics describe what makes financial information useful. Two are fundamental: information must be relevant and a faithful representation.
it can make a difference to a decision, for example by helping a user predict the future or check past results.
it shows what really happened, in a complete, neutral way and free from error.
information is better when it is comparable (can be set beside other years or businesses), verifiable (others can check it), timely (available in time to be used) and understandable (clear to users).
draft.remember: Useful information is relevant and a faithful representation. Comparable, verifiable, timely and understandable make it better.

a.q: A bank manager reads a business's report and finds it shows the true position, complete and without bias. Which characteristic is this?
a.why: Showing what really happened in a complete and neutral way is faithful representation. Relevance is about making a difference to a decision, not about whether the report is accurate.
a.clue: Think about whether the report matches what really happened.

b.q: Jarrah Hardware in Bendigo gives its owner the June sales report in November, after the owner has already chosen to hire more staff. Which characteristic is the report mainly lacking?
b.why: The report arrived after the decision was made, so it could not be used. That is a lack of timeliness. Relevance is also affected, but timeliness is the enhancing characteristic that explains the problem here.
b.clue: When did the owner need the information?
